$comment: The interop contract: every attribute a component OTHER THAN THE EMITTER reads.
Vendored, and intended to be byte-identical in both repositories.
Hand-authored, not generated, and deliberately so. A generator over beckn-onix
would have to AST-walk literal call sites in stdHandler.go and var declarations
in pluginMetrics.go, and a generator whose input is string literals ratifies
whatever was last typed — including a typo — the moment it is regenerated.
Sixteen reviewed rows is the right size for a file whose whole value is that a
human agreed to it.
What this file catches: a rename inside one repository. What it does NOT catch:
both repositories holding stale copies of it, in which case our test passes
green and spans silently stop stitching. telemetry-seam.md 5g ranks the three
mitigations, and additive-only aliasing is the only one that removes the failure
mode rather than detecting it. Any claim that this file prevents cross-repo
drift is wrong.
Explicitly NOT here: onix's onix_step_* and onix_plugin_* internals, which
nothing of ours reads; and our sender.unverified / sender.unidentified, which
are a policy the facilitator has not responded to. A key earns a row by being
read across a boundary, not by being important.
Pinned to a tag rather than a bare commit. v1.8.2 is the newest valid semver
on beckn-onix — its v2.0 tags are not valid semver and are unresolvable.
telemetry-seam.md open item 3 proposes moving this file's home to
network-telemetry-spec/schemas/, which both repositories already treat as
normative. Propose it; it does not block anything here.

attributes.note: API for spans, METRIC for metrics, AUDIT — not LOG — for log records. The one Resource attribute that varies per signal.
The participant id, an FQDN. Distinct from service.name, which is not in this contract because it is ClickStack's grouping column and nothing across a boundary reads it.
The sector. Required by the spec on all three signals, which is why the Resource is constructed once.
Ours rather than the spec's, but read by the network layer, so its spelling is no longer ours alone.

I1. beckn-onix's network collector rewrites trace_id from an attribute named literally this (otel-collector-network/config.yaml:23-25). A span spelled beckn.transactionId alone is never stitched to anything.

I1, and a searchable tag rather than a join: the collector deliberately does not map it onto span_id, because several nodes emit spans for one Beckn message and identical span ids would corrupt the trace.

Optional here — participant identity was parked with Task 6 — and beckn-onix's filter/network_traces drops every span where it is nil (node/otel-collector-bap/config.yaml:29-33). That is U2, onix's bug to fix by filtering on transaction_id, which is what the pipeline downstream actually consumes. Do not synthesise a value to buy admission.

Who answered. beckn-onix's spans use this spelling (pluginMetrics.go:49, stdHandler.go:855); receiver.id appears there only on audit-log records and no collector pipeline reads it off a span, so there is no alias for it here. One capital letter from beckn.receiverId, which means the opposite — the caller's claim about who it addressed.
Generated per span in a SpanProcessor's OnStart.
Unix nanos as a string. The spec's prose says ISO; its field name and examples say nanos, and the name wins.
Part of the spec's mandatory span profile, so a facilitator reads it.
Part of the spec's mandatory span profile.

Both sides spell the key identically; the divergence is in the value. We emit the route template, the spec's prose says URL. That is a value-derivation decision recorded on the Definition, not a naming disagreement.

Required by the spec's mandatory span profile (otel-specification.md:307), so a facilitator reads it. On the ALIAS rather than the SpanKey, because the spec disagrees with itself on the type — its structure says Int, all three examples emit a string — and we follow the examples here while keeping the int on http.status_code for ClickStack. The contract covers the spelling the facilitator reads; the local one is ours.
No Definition owns it yet. It stays in the contract because the contract is the interop surface, not our build order.
